meaning: Owner decision 2026-11-06 (#1010): who fixes the grammar, covered by cases. In the authority cell, the open case bridge yields the definition bridge, and the two earlier defeats apply (WF-FAILS-AS-DESCRIPTION-OF-CATHOLIC-PRACTICE from Dei Filius can. II.1, FIDEIST-REFERENCE-BUNDLE-FAILS-FOR-CATHOLIC-PRACTICE from can. I.1), composed by importing their theorems. In the ordinary-use cell, the open case bridge makes ordinary-use moves the practice's own standard; with the evidence premises that ordinary use affirms natural knowability (supported: CCC 31-38 in the official English translation) and confesses the one true God (supported by the creed's first article and CCC 185-189, 199-200), both fideist bundles fail. With FIDEISM-GRAMMAR-CASES-PARTITION, the remaining cell is grammar fixed by neither: neitherCellSurvives certifies that both bundles survive there with every premise. needsAuthorityCaseBridge and needsUseCaseBridge show the case bridges are needed. Status: premises open (the shared-reason reading, both case bridges), supported (both ordinary-use evidence premises), stated (the two canons); none established, so no refutes relation (#999). So: the fideist descriptive thesis fails whichever of the practice's own fixers fixes its grammar, conditionally on those premises; it survives only if neither does.

strong_version_needed.STMT-DEI-FILIUS-DEFINES-NATURAL-KNOWABIL: The original cut-off derivation/authority branch needs the same actual move to be both Defined and natural-knowability: Defined supplies own-standard endorsement/correctness through the definition bridge, while natural content supplies shared reason. The weak merely-natural witness omits Defined, and the weak merely-Defined witness omits natural content; separate existential witnesses do not identify the same move. The original interface therefore retains the joint defined-natural witness.
